Data.title: Ukraine Passes Bill to Legalize Bitcoin and Crypto, Sets 18% Tax on Gains
Data.body: Ukraine’s parliament voted on Wednesday to legalize the country’s crypto market, with 271 lawmakers backing the bill. The vote passed bill No. 10225-d in its second reading, with eight lawmakers against. The Verkhovna Rada announced the vote on its official Telegram channel. The bill takes effect on July 1, 2027, and still needs President Volodymyr Zelensky’s signature. Parliament passed an earlier law, On Virtual Assets, in February 2022. It named the securities commission and the central bank as regulators when Zelensky signed it in March 2022. It is still listed as not in force in Ukraine’s official legislation database. Its final provisions begin only once a law amending the Tax Code on crypto taxation takes effect. The new bill amends the Tax Code to set out how crypto is taxed. Yaroslav Zhelezniak, first deputy chair of parliament’s finance committee, expects the law to raise an extra UAH 15 billion in budget revenue. In 2023, Ukraine’s Economic Security Bureau said unregulated local exchanges had cost the state UAH 3 billion in uncollected taxes. “Finally, we have done what was not possible for 35 years,” Zhelezniak wrote on Telegram. Older Holdings Taxed on Full Sales Individuals will pay 18% personal income tax and a 5% military levy on crypto profits. Swaps between crypto assets are not taxed, and neither is annual profit up to one minimum wage. Crypto bought before the law takes effect gets a lower rate through 2028. Those holders will pay 5% income tax plus the military levy on the entire amount sold, Zhelezniak said. Lawmakers backed the first-reading version on September 3, 2025, with 246 votes. That draft was due to start on January 1, 2026. It allowed the lower rate only on assets sold during that year. Central Bank Gets Stablecoin Powers The National Securities and Stock Market Commission (NSSMC) becomes the market’s main regulator. The commission will oversee which exchanges, custodians, and other providers are admitted to the market. They must also report Ukrainian residents’ transactions every year. The National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) takes charge of stablecoins and can allow or ban their circulation. Bybit’s 2025 adoption report counted more than $6.9 billion in stablecoin flows through Ukraine, against a $190 billion economy. The finance committee cleared the bill for second reading on November 4. A day later, the NBU said it could not support that version, citing risks to monetary sovereignty, financial stability and competition. The committee reviewed the text again on November 23, when the NBU and the NSSMC agreed on their positions. It then backed the bill unanimously. Data.title: Franklin Templeton Will Add HYPE to Its Eight High-Yield Crypto ETFs on December 1
Data.body: Franklin Templeton’s crypto index ETF is preparing to add Hyperliquid’s HYPE token to its portfolio. According to a prospectus filed with the SEC today by Franklin Crypto Trust, HYPE’s inclusion in the tracked index will take effect on December 1, 2026. The change stems from the composition of the CF Institutional Digital Asset Index, which the Franklin Crypto Index ETF tracks. Index provider CF Benchmarks has identified HYPE as a new component. The fund will also adjust its portfolio according to the index weights. With the addition of HYPE, the fund’s scope will expand to eight crypto assets. Alongside Bitcoin and Ethereum, XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, Cardano, and Stellar will also be included in the same investment portfolio. This will allow investors to access the price movements of all eight assets through a single exchange-traded fund. The investment universe of the existing multi-asset product is expanding; the share allocated to HYPE will be determined by the weighting of the index. The document anticipates the portfolio being adjusted to the new composition around December 1st. The significance of this development for HYPE lies in the fact that the token will be included in the regular portfolio allocation of a US-traded crypto index product. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: If You Hold Crypto In France, Senate Rejects €100,000 Wallet Reporting Rule
Data.body: France’s Senate rejected two proposals on Nov. 24, 2026, that would have required taxpayers to declare self-custody crypto wallets holding a combined €100,000 or more. The test used the value on Dec. 31, even if the holder had sold nothing. The vote keeps the rule out of the Senate’s 2027 budget text. People with accounts on foreign crypto platforms still have to declare those accounts; the rejected rule concerned wallets they manage themselves. The amendments would have applied to crypto held outside a service provider. In its proposal , the Communist-led CRCE-K group argued that taxpayers could keep substantial holdings beyond the tax authority’s view: Wallets that the holder manages themselves, without an intermediary, escape any obligation. CRCE-K group amendment (translated from French) Sen. Anne-Sophie Romagny and seven other senators submitted an identical reporting rule . The National Assembly approved the measure on Nov. 3, but it fell away when lawmakers rejected the budget’s entire revenue section the next day. Both versions failed in the Senate after the government and the Senate’s finance committee opposed them. Budget Minister David Amiel said the EU’s DAC8 rules already require crypto service providers to report users’ transactions to tax authorities. He argued that a declaration of wallet holdings alone would not show authorities how crypto was used in money laundering or tax fraud. Senators also rejected a proposal to tax swaps into certain regulated stablecoins , tokens designed to hold a steady value. They rejected an extension of France’s exit tax to unrealized crypto gains when qualifying taxpayers move their tax residence abroad. A separate amendment still pending would raise the fine for refusing a tax authority’s information request from €10,000 to €50,000 per request for institutions including crypto service providers. The wallet rule could return during negotiations before the budget’s final adoption. The Senate is scheduled to vote on the full budget on Dec. 9. Data.title: XRP Exchange Reserves Disappearing. Here’s What Happened
Data.body: Something is shifting in the XRP market. Crypto commentator Digital Asset Investor (@digitalassetbuy) highlighted on-chain data showing XRP reserves falling across several major exchanges. He drew from a post by BankXRP (@BankXRP), who compiled the reserve figures and paired them with a CryptoQuant chart. XRP’s price has been falling , but the data paints a picture that goes beyond the current market dip. What Digital Asset Investor Said Digital Asset Investor confirmed the market decline but kept his focus on the reserve data. He said the drop in exchange reserves is “something worth watching.” He noted that less XRP on exchanges “normally means good things.” When tokens leave exchanges, it typically signals that holders are moving assets to self-custody rather than positioning to sell. XRP Exchange Reserves Dropping pic.twitter.com/cxkgUnlAjO — Digital Asset Investor (@digitalassetbuy) November 24, 2026 The Reserve Numbers BankXRP published the specific figures driving the conversation. Binance currently holds 2.4 billion XRP. Upbit holds 6.4 billion XRP. Bithumb holds 1.75 billion XRP. His post states that the exchange reserves are dropping sharply even as the broader market declines. He also called it something worth watching. Details From the Chart The CryptoQuant chart BankXRP shared tracks XRP reserves across eight exchanges from mid-2025 through November 2026. It includes Binance, Upbit, and Bithumb. The chart plots each exchange’s reserve line alongside the XRP price line in black. Upbit, shown in blue, carries the largest reserve at 6.4 billion XRP and has held near the top of the chart throughout the tracked period. Bithumb, in red, sits at 1.75 billion XRP. Binance, in orange, shows 2.4 billion XRP and displays a notable decline in recent months. The XRP price line sits near $0.944, after a brief recovery from its recent two-year low . The chart shows a pullback in recent months alongside the reserve drops. What the Reserve Decline Signals Falling exchange reserves are a closely tracked metric in crypto markets. When holders withdraw tokens from exchanges , it reduces the available supply for immediate sale. That reduction in sell-side liquidity has historically preceded price recoveries, though it does not guarantee one. The data across multiple exchanges strengthens the signal. A drop on a single exchange could reflect platform-specific activity. Drops across Binance, Upbit, and Bithumb simultaneously suggest a wider pattern of accumulation or self-custody. Digital Asset Investor and BankXRP believe these numbers are worth watching, and the data supports that assessment. Data.title: Why is Crypto Down Today? BTC Under $60K: How Low Will It Go?
Data.body: Why is crypto down again? The cryptocurrency market is firmly in the red on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. Total market capitalization has slipped to around $2.02 trillion, down roughly 1.8–2% over the past 24 hours, while the Fear & Greed Index sits deep in Extreme Fear territory near 13/100. Traders are growing disillusioned with the crypto market after weeks of downside sell pressure that has seen Bitcoin crash nearly -30% to under $60,000. Many are left wondering what could reverse the market’s course as we head toward 2027. How are the Major Tokens Performing Right Now? Bitcoin (BTC) is trading near $58,000–$58,400, down approximately 3% on the day and struggling to regain the $60,000 level after briefly testing higher earlier in the week. Ethereum (ETH) sits around $1,630–$1,640, off about 3.3–3.5%. Solana (SOL) is softer still at roughly $66.80–$67.30, down around 4%. XRP is near $0.89–$0.90 (down ~2.5%), and BNB trades around $533–$536 (down ~2.5%). Most other large-cap altcoins are also lower, reflecting weak market breadth. These levels follow Bitcoin’s failure to hold gains sparked by the recent Nvidia-related rebound, leaving the market on the back foot heading into month-end. Why Is Crypto Down Today? THE MARKET IS CRASHING The Nasdaq is down over 3%, the S&P 500 over 2% and Nvidia about 8%, all within minutes of the open. The VIX is back above 30. Here's why: 1. New tariffs The Trump administration just announced 20% tariffs on China, the EU and 12 other countries.… pic.twitter.com/JeWavoJwQC — NoLimit (@NoLimitGains) November 25, 2026 The primary driver remains persistent institutional selling through U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs. November has already set a record for monthly outflows, with figures ranging from about $4.71Bn to nearly $5Bn depending on the data provider. BlackRock’s IBIT has led the redemptions on multiple sessions, including large single-day withdrawals exceeding $500M earlier in the week and continued outflows of roughly $230M more recently. What was once a reliable source of demand has flipped into a consistent headwind. Broader risk-off sentiment is amplifying the pressure. A sharp sell-off in Asian markets, including a roughly 6% drop in South Korea’s KOSPI and heavy losses for SoftBank, spilled into global risk assets. Technology and AI-related stocks, which had briefly rallied on news of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, quickly faded. Crypto continues to trade as a high-beta risk asset, moving closely with equities as investor risk appetite contracts. Macro factors are also weighing heavily. Markets are pricing in high odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, with elevated Treasury yields reducing the relative appeal of non-yielding assets like Bitcoin. Reports of potential new U.S. tariffs targeting multiple trading partners have added another layer of uncertainty. Thin liquidity around the Thanksgiving holiday period may also be magnifying moves. In short, the market faces a classic mix of sustained ETF outflows, cooling equity momentum, tighter monetary-policy expectations, and residual geopolitical/trade noise. Sentiment has deteriorated to the point where any bounce is being sold rather than chased. What Could Reverse the Course for Crypto? Despite the heavy atmosphere, several catalysts could stabilize or reverse the decline. Today’s U.S. economic data, particularly PCE inflation and GDP figures, will be closely watched. Softer-than-expected readings that reduce the probability of aggressive Fed tightening could quickly improve risk appetite across stocks and crypto. A slowdown or reversal in ETF outflows would be an important positive signal. Even a return to modest net inflows would suggest institutional selling is exhausting and that larger players are beginning to accumulate at these lower levels. On-chain data has already shown some large-wallet accumulation in recent weeks even as ETF products bled, hinting that longer-term holders may be positioning ahead of a potential recovery. Major Cap Technical Analysis: How Cooked Are BTC and ETH? Bitcoin (BTC) 24h 7d 30d 1y All time Bitcoin and Ethereum look deeply oversold on shorter timeframes, with RSI readings in the low-to-mid 20s in some analyses. Extreme fear readings have historically preceded relief rallies, especially when price approaches prior support zones. Any constructive regulatory development, clearer institutional adoption news, or a rebound in technology stocks could also help shift momentum. Thinner holiday liquidity means volatility is likely to remain elevated in either direction. While the near-term setup remains cautious and further downside is possible if risk assets continue to weaken, extreme sentiment, oversold technical conditions, and potential macro relief provide a plausible path to stabilization once the current wave of selling pressure eases. Crypto markets have repeatedly demonstrated resilience after periods of heavy institutional outflows and macro headwinds; whether that pattern reasserts itself in the coming sessions will depend heavily on the data and a shift in broader risk appetite. Data.title: Bitcoin Recovery: What Seven Previous Market Lows Tell Investors
Data.body: The plunge on November 21 that took Bitcoin to around $55,000 may have marked a market low, with historical data shared by CF Benchmarks showing that five of seven comparable sell-offs since April 2024 were followed by higher prices a month later. However, the analysis also warned that the three-month record is far less encouraging, which leaves open the possibility that the latest recovery is just a temporary open. Bitcoin Washout Signals Point to a Possible Recovery CF Benchmarks published a report on X that examined the extreme market conditions surrounding Bitcoin’s November sell-off and compared them with seven other episodes from the past. According to the research firm, around the time BTC plummeted, the stress was visible across several indicators, including the CME’s CF Bitcoin Volatility Index Settlement Rate (BVXS), which, on November 20, closed at 52.83 to record a rolling 30-day z-score of 3.30. A z-score measures how far a reading sits above or below its recent average, and that was its eighth-highest reading across 635 sessions. Meanwhile, nearly 83% of CF Broad Cap Index constituents closed at 90-day lows, with every one of them trading below their 20-day and 50-day moving averages. And on November 21, BTC’s real-time reference price touched $55,153, with implied volatility then reaching 71.83. The analysis then looked at market data going back to April 2024 and identified seven other times when at least 80% of the constituents in its Broad Cap Index reached 90-day lows, and using the first day of each cluster as the starting point, tracked how Bitcoin had performed one and three months later. Results from the one-month checks showed that in five of the seven cases, BTC finished higher, with the median return at about 5.5%. However, those rebounds didn’t always come immediately, with the OG crypto first dipping by another 5% or so below its starting price in four episodes, the median worst dip being 8.4%. This time, Saturday’s lowest hourly reading, when Bitcoin went to $55,000, was 7.2%. In the 3-month picture, four of the seven episodes also ended higher and produced a median gain of 10%. And while outcomes ranged from a loss of 28.6% to a 37.3% gain, two signals from November 2025 eventually ended in much deeper lows after 77 and 92 days. What Could Confirm a Low Monday’s reference price of about $63,000 sat over 14% above the weekend bottom, but that bounce has since faded. As CryptoPotato reported, BTC went as high as $64,500 after global markets were lifted by the Nvidia board reinstating CEO Jensen Huang. But it then slipped under $60,000, with CoinGecko data at the time of writing showing the asset changing hands around $58,600 after a decline of more than 2% in 24 hours. Bitcoin is also 8% lower than where it was a week ago and over 26% from its price from 30 days ago. The year-on-year drop is at around 33%, which has helped keep the flagship cryptocurrency 53% below its all-time high. To confirm a low, CF Benchmarks says there should be fewer tokens setting 90-day lows, alongside BVXS going back to its October norm. Furthermore, the index provider wants the Broad Cap Index, recorded at 2,092.89 on Monday, to hold above 2,018.60. For BTC, it says the support zone to watch goes from $55,000 to $58,300. Data.title: ARB Drops 20% in a Week Even as Variational Pushes $59B of Perps Through Arbitrum
Data.body: Three Things to Know A single protocol now handles almost all perpetual futures trading on Arbitrum, yet ARB keeps sliding. The daily RSI sits deep in oversold territory while sellers still control the trend. Bulls need a close above the first resistance before any bounce earns trust. Variational has turned Arbitrum into one of the busiest perp venues in crypto, with DefiLlama data showing nearly all of the chain's derivatives flow running through its zero-fee Omni product. The ARB token has moved the other way, sinking to its weakest level in almost three months. That gap raises a hard question for holders: whether record network activity can ever reach the token. One Protocol Now Carries Nearly All of Arbitrum's Perp Flow Variational, an on-chain derivatives protocol built on Arbitrum, processed about $59.3 billion in perpetual futures volume over the past 30 days, DefiLlama data shows. All of that flow ran on Arbitrum, whose total 30-day perp volume came to roughly $61.6 billion. One venue now accounts for almost the entire market. Daily figures look similar. Arbitrum logged about $1.89 billion in perp volume on Nov. 23, and Variational handled roughly $1.8 billion of it. GMX did about $36 million, while Aark Digital managed around $33 million. This run has been building for months. Variational logged more than $34 billion in volume in September. A later tally put it near $66.4 billion, enough to rank third among perps venues behind Hyperliquid and Lighter. Most of that traffic comes through Omni, the protocol's retail product. Omni charges zero trading fees and lists more than 500 markets. It uses a request-for-quote design with a single professional liquidity provider, and the protocol earns from the spread. Growth picked up after Variational added gold, silver, copper and oil perps in May. U.S. stocks now drive three of Omni's five busiest markets. Volume alone does not prove the business is profitable or that the pace will last. The token has not shared in the activity either. ARB fell 20% over the week, more than double Bitcoin's 9% drop, and trades near an 86-day low. Record Volume Fails to Lift ARB Off Its Lows Arbitrum (ARB) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView ARB changed hands near $0.11 on Monday, down about 3% on the day. The modest move added another step to a decline that has run for weeks without a single sharp flush. That pattern matters for anyone hoping for a bottom. Capitulation usually shows up as one violent day of forced selling, followed by a quick rebound. ARB has instead bled lower in small, steady pieces, which suggests sellers are still unloading at their own pace. The token is down roughly 37% over the past month. That stretch overlaps with Variational's heaviest trading on Arbitrum. The chain is busier than ever, yet the token's holders have little to show for it. The perp flow pays traders and the liquidity provider, and none of that value is routed back to ARB. Moving averages point the same way. The 50-day average, which tracks the past ten weeks of prices, sits near $0.15. The 200-day average, a gauge of the longer trend, has slid down to the same level. When both lines meet at one price, they form a single, heavier ceiling. ARB trades about a quarter below it. Any rally would have to climb that full distance before buyers could claim the trend had turned. Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Sellers RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 26 on daily timeframes. Readings under 30 count as oversold. That means the selling has run hard and fast, and a short relief bounce can come from levels like these. Oversold is a warning sign for sellers. It is not a buy signal. Tokens can stay stretched for days or weeks when a downtrend has real force behind it. ARB's trend has that force. Trend-strength readings show a genuine directional move, and sellers are the side driving it. Momentum also still points down. The RSI says the drop is overdone. The other gauges say nobody has stepped in to stop it yet. Traders waiting for a turn would want to see momentum flatten first, before any bounce earns much trust. Why $0.12 Is the First Test for Any Bounce The first line overhead sits near $0.12, marked in red. A modest bounce could reach it quickly. Closing a day above it would be the first real sign that sellers are tiring. The next resistance lines up with the merged moving averages flagged earlier. That ceiling is the bigger hurdle, and buyers would need sustained volume to break through it. The downside map is thinner. Support shows up near $0.083, drawn in green. That floor sits well below today's price, leaving a wide gap the token could fall through with little in the way. Below that level, the data shows no further support at all. A break there would leave ARB in open space, with no recent price history to slow the fall. Relief Rally or Another Leg Lower The first resistance line decides between two paths. Bullish: A daily close above that first red line would open a run toward the merged 50-day and 200-day averages. The setup fails if ARB slips back under today's price, which would put sellers back in charge. Bearish: A rejection at the first resistance would likely send the token down toward the green support line. A finish above that resistance would invalidate this case. Activity Alone Will Not Rescue the Token Until the token reclaims that first resistance line, any bounce is a relief move inside a downtrend. The network story carries its own risk. Nearly all of Arbitrum's perp flow depends on one protocol and one liquidity provider. If either pulls back, the record activity could thin out fast.
